focus: Design the long-lived /doctor:update environment: worktree creation, overlay, four unit statuses, sk-code choice, Barter sk-git plan, commit/record-base requirements and reset.
answeredQuestions: How can a long-lived local /doctor:update environment exercise customized, conflict, removed and local-only units across record-base/check/align/apply/rollback, including release-tag and worktree constraints?
noveltyJustification: The updater's unit enumeration, classification, base and rollback mechanics plus the sk-git allocator rules give a complete fixture design with deterministic statuses; only the Barter file overlap remains UNKNOWN.
keyQuestions: How can a long-lived local /doctor:update environment exercise customized, conflict, removed and local-only units across record-base/check/align/apply/rollback, including release-tag and worktree constraints?

label: Create the environment with the sk-git allocator as a numbered named worktree: `worktree-naming.sh create doctor-update-test-environment v4.0.0.0 --no-provision` -> branch worktrees/{NNN}-doctor-update-test-environment and dir .worktrees/{NNN}-...; the literal .doctor-update-test-environment name is outside the validated grammar. Use the named branch lane, not detached HEAD, because overrides must be committed and apply refuses dirty targets.

Tags v4.0.0.0 and v4.0.0.2 carry only the legacy doctor-update.yaml, so overlay the current update.md, _routes.yaml, doctor-update-presentation.txt, five action YAMLs and scripts/release-update.cjs. The overlay groups into the single unit command:commands/doctor, which must stay out of assertion scopes.

Fixtures: customized = sk-code/sk-code-webflow (SKILL.md identical across tags, changelogs release-changed); conflict = sk-git after Barter replacement with a release-changed path forced to differ locally; removed = sk-code-obsidian under a local prerelease tag; local = new sk-code/sk-code-web-dev packet absent from base and release. New files must be git-added because local enumeration starts from the index.

Prefer adding the derived sk-code-web-dev packet over stripping modes to sk-code-opencode and sk-code-webflow. Stripping breaks the hub's declared two-axis contract, deletes units with mixed local/conflict classes, and forces router/registry/manifest edits; the new packet yields exactly one local unit with no hub edits.

Commit the fixture baseline: apply refuses planned targets dirty against HEAD and record-base refuses a dirty base.json (.skilled/release/base.json). Offline record-base of v4.0.0.0 needs --trust-release and reports verified:false; then commit base.json before any further action.

Reset after apply with rollback --run=<runDir>: it restores before states, deletes added files, restores base.json/divergence.json, reports skipped paths with exit 1, and clears the lock. Re-apply of the same run is refused once rollback.json exists; run align again for a new plan.

The Barter sk-git snapshot is absent from this checkout, so its 10-file overlap with the tags is UNKNOWN. Plan: replace the fixture sk-git tree with the Barter files, force one release-changed path (references/finish-workflows.md or scripts/worktree-naming.sh) to differ locally for a deterministic conflict, and create the worktree before the replacement because the replacement removes the fixture's own allocator.
